events.title: Gunfight at the O.K. Corral
events.description: In Tombstone, Arizona Territory, Wyatt Earp, his brothers Virgil and Morgan, and Doc Holliday fought the Clanton-McLaury cowboys in a roughly 30-second gunfight that left three of the cowboys dead.
events.significance: The shootout became one of the most famous events of the American Old West and a lasting symbol of frontier violence and law enforcement myth-making.

events.title: Founding of the Football Association's Predecessor Meeting
events.description: Representatives of London-area clubs met at the Freemasons' Tavern and formed The Football Association, beginning the process of codifying the rules of association football.
events.significance: The meeting established the first governing body of football and set the foundation for the modern rules of the world's most popular sport.

events.title: Israel-Jordan Peace Treaty Signed
events.description: Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin and Jordanian Prime Minister Abdelsalam al-Majali signed a peace treaty at the Arava/Araba border crossing, witnessed by U.S. President Bill Clinton, formally ending the state of war between the two countries.
events.significance: Jordan became the second Arab country, after Egypt, to make peace with Israel, establishing diplomatic relations and resolving border and water disputes.

events.title: Ottoman Empire Enters World War I
events.description: Ottoman warships under German command bombarded Russian Black Sea ports on October 29, following earlier steps, while on October 26 Ottoman leadership finalized war planning with Germany that led to the empire joining the Central Powers.
events.significance: The Ottoman entry widened World War I into the Middle East and ultimately contributed to the collapse of the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: USA PATRIOT Act Signed into Law
events.description: President George W. Bush signed the USA PATRIOT Act, passed in response to the September 11 attacks, expanding the surveillance and investigative powers of U.S. law enforcement and intelligence agencies.
events.significance: The act reshaped the balance between national security and civil liberties in the United States and remains the subject of ongoing debate.
